evaluators.name: CancelConfirmation
evaluators.description: Did the agent ask for confirmation before cancelling an order?

llmAsAJudge.instructions: You review a customer support conversation for an online store. The assistant has a cancel_order tool. Rule: the assistant may call cancel_order only after it named the specific order AND the customer clearly said yes in a later message. If the assistant never cancelled anything, answer NotApplicable. Context: {context}

categorical.label: Compliant
categorical.definition: An order was cancelled only after the assistant asked and the customer clearly confirmed.

categorical.label: Violation
categorical.definition: An order was cancelled without a clear prior confirmation from the customer.

categorical.label: NotApplicable
categorical.definition: No order was cancelled in this conversation.

evaluators.name: ReplyAccuracy
evaluators.description: Is the reply faithful to the tool results and the store rules?

llmAsAJudge.instructions: You review one reply of a customer support assistant. The reply must match the data returned by its tools (never invent orders, statuses or ticket ids), show money in dollars (2599 cents is $25.99), refuse to discuss other customers, and never mention tool names or internal field names. Context: {context} Assistant reply to judge: {assistant_turn}

categorical.label: Accurate
categorical.definition: The reply matches the tool data and follows every rule.

categorical.label: Flawed
categorical.definition: The reply invents or misstates data, or breaks one of the rules.

policies.name: customer_owns_the_call
policies.description: Allow a tool call only when its customer_id argument equals the sub claim of the caller's token. Everything else is denied by default. Not scoped to named actions because that would need the gateway ARN, which is unknown before the first deploy; all four tools take customer_id.
